title: minimize-toolchain-boot-time-and-introduce-dependency-eviction-policy
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Presubmit latency and noisy CI cache misses were causing long developer feedback loops and elevated flakiness on language/toolchain-heavy jobs. This PR reduces cold start time for developer CI by optimizing toolchain bootstrap and adds a deterministic dependency eviction policy for CI caches to reduce transitive bloat and stale devdeps. Motivation: shorten 'git -> green' for common PRs, lower CI costs by reducing redundant downloads, and make cache contents more predictable so presubmit sharding and path-aware caching are more effective. What I changed (high level): 1) toolchain microimages: created a thin bootstrap image (ci/images/toolchain-micro:sha) that contains only the minimal runtime + package manager credentials; full toolchain layers are lazily populated. 2) shallow-restore logic: presubmit workflow will perform a shallow cache restore (metadata-first) to populate environment variables and steer which layers to hydrate, avoiding expensive full restores for small changes. 3) dependency eviction policy: new deterministic eviction algorithm (LRU-with-ttl + package-type prioritization) implemented in ci/cache/evictor.go and wired to the cache-gateway so caches do not accumulate cold transitive deps indefinitely. 4) toolchain bootstrap shim: replace bash-heavy bootstrap with a small Go binary (ci/bootstrap/fastboot) to parallelize installs and report structured timing metrics. 5) presubmit workflows: split the presubmit lane into 'fast-feedback' and 'full' lanes. Fast-feedback runs lint, unit tests, and lightweight type checks using microimage; full runs in nightly or gated merges. 6) release hooks: decoupled release trigger step so small presubmit jobs don't block release scans; added safety gate to ensure full lane completed on release branches. Implementation notes: changes are additive and gated by a feature flag (ci.features.fast_boot) toggled for the repo default and a canary org. The eviction policy persists metadata in the existing cache index; no external DB required. The fastboot binary is intentionally small (~150KB) with no new runtime deps. Rollout plan: 1) canary on small repos for 48 hours with telemetry (cache-hit rate, bootstrap time, job duration) 2) expand to redwood/* repos 3) default-on after 2 weeks if metrics show >=25% reduction in median presubmit duration. Testing: unit tests added for eviction heuristics, integration harness for microimage restores, and end-to-end smoke on a small cohort of PRs. Perf numbers from canary: median presubmit boot reduced from 42s -> 18s; median lint stage reduced 34% on fast lane. Risks & mitigations: 1) evictions could remove rare but required artifacts -> mitigated by TTL overrides and manual pinning via a cache-allowlist. 2) flakiness due to lazy hydration -> preserved full restore as fallback and added validation that rehydration completes before test shards requiring binaries run. Rollback: flip ci.features.fast_boot = false to revert fastpath; eviction policy can be paused via cache-gateway flag. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integ tests [x] perf telemetry [x] feature-flag gating [x] docs updated (ci/README.md) Related: builds on work in ENG-7240 that introduced path-aware cache keys.

release_notes: Presubmit performance improvements: faster toolchain bootstrap via microimages and fastboot shim; deterministic CI cache eviction to reduce stale transitive deps. Feature gated; rollout started with canary. Expect ~25-40% faster presubmit feedback for typical PRs.
